title: Arai Eek CoLabs
description: CoLabs Chiang Mai was an interdisciplinary residency and collaborative learning program that brought together artists, designers, scientists, educators, and community practitioners from across world to explore the intersections of art, science, technology, and local knowledge. Through workshops, open laboratories, field research, collective discussions, and hands-on experimentation, participants engaged with DIY and DIWO methodologies while developing projects rooted in collaboration and knowledge sharing. The residency fostered an environment where cultural exchange, critical inquiry, and creative exploration unfolded through everyday interactions, encouraging participants to rethink the relationship between technology, ecology, community, and artistic practice. For Muhammad Zeian, the program offered valuable opportunities to expand his interdisciplinary perspective and strengthen his engagement with collaborative and open-source approaches to art-making.

title: Peripheral Cartography East Java and Japan
exhibition: Japan Foundation × Biennale Jatim, Surabaya, Indonesia
description: Kartografi Pinggiran was a three-day curatorial workshop that brought together eleven artists and cultural practitioners from across East Java to explore how local narratives, cultural practices, and peripheral perspectives can be mapped, interpreted, and represented beyond dominant urban centers. Facilitated by Yuki Hatori, Ismal Muntaha, and Elyda K. Rara with support from the Japan Foundation Jakarta, the program combined discussions, case studies, collaborative mapping exercises, proposal mentoring, and participant presentations. Through critical conversations on locality, representation, community relations, and curatorial positioning, participants were encouraged to develop curatorial proposals rooted in their own contexts while reflecting on the ethical dimensions of cultural mediation. The workshop fostered a space for collective learning, exchange, and long-term collaboration, emphasizing curation as a practice of listening, nurturing relationships, and sustaining local cultural knowledge.

title: Napak Teles
description: Napak Teles is a speculative artistic project that reinterprets local folklore through contemporary storytelling, performance, and technological imagination. Drawing from the journey of Sindujoyo and his encounter with Salam and Salim, the work reconstructs fragments of legend through a fictional expedition across the Madura Strait, where historical traces, myths, and everyday objects intersect in unexpected ways. The project culminates in Vulkano 3D Printing, a conceptual venture imagined as a contemporary continuation of Salam and Salim's journey, transforming human faces into three-dimensional objects through digital fabrication technologies. By weaving together oral history, humor, local narratives, and emerging technologies, the project explores how folklore can be continuously reimagined and activated within present-day cultural and technological landscapes.

title: MTN Lab Gresik
description: *MTN Lab: Residency* was a talent development program within the National Talent Management (MTN) trajectory for Visual Arts, designed as a platform for learning, experimentation, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Conceived not merely as a physical laboratory but as a space for process and exploration, the program brought together emerging artists, mentors, and experts from diverse fields through residencies, workshops, masterclasses, incubation sessions, and collaborative projects. Participants were encouraged to develop their artistic ideas, expand their professional networks, and engage with local contexts while reflecting on broader national and global issues. Through this dynamic environment of exchange and creative inquiry, *MTN Lab: Residency* fostered the growth of new artistic practices rooted in experimentation, critical thinking, and cross-disciplinary dialogue.

title: Grissee Open Lab
description: Grissee Open Lab 2024 was an experimental learning platform initiated by Arcolabs and curated by Nabila Warda, bringing together artists, makers, researchers, and creative practitioners through a series of workshops, presentations, collaborative projects, and open discussions. Designed as a space for interdisciplinary exchange, the program encouraged participants to explore contemporary art, technology, and community-based practices through hands-on experimentation and collective inquiry. By fostering collaboration across different fields and backgrounds, the open lab created opportunities for participants to share knowledge, develop new ideas, and build meaningful connections within an evolving ecosystem of art, science, and technology.

title: HAIOKU Artist in Residency
description: HAIOKU Artist in Residency provided Muhammad Zeian with an opportunity to engage in an experimental environment where artistic practice intersected with architecture, urbanism, and adaptive reuse. Hosted by Nishimura-Gumi and HAIOKU LLC in Japan, the residency brought together artists, architects, musicians, DJs, and cultural practitioners from diverse backgrounds to explore new possibilities for abandoned buildings through collective living, research, and creative intervention. Working within spaces undergoing transformation, Zeian participated in an ongoing dialogue about how neglected structures can be reimagined as sites of cultural production, community engagement, and artistic experimentation. The residency expanded his perspective on spatial practice, collaboration, and the potential of art as a catalyst for generating new values within existing urban environments.

title: TUAK (Terbuka Untuk Aku dan Kamu) Residency
description: TUAK (Terbuka Untuk Aku dan Kamu) was a collaborative residency and learning platform that brought together artists, makers, researchers, and community practitioners through a series of workshops, discussions, and hands-on experiments. Rooted in the DIY and DIWO philosophies championed by the Hackteria network, the program fostered interdisciplinary exchange across art, science, technology, and local knowledge systems. Through collective making, open-ended research, and informal knowledge sharing, participants were encouraged to develop new ideas, build meaningful collaborations, and explore alternative approaches to creative practice. The residency created a space where experimentation, curiosity, and mutual learning became catalysts for both personal growth and collective innovation.

title: Lifepatch Residency
description: Through multiple residency periods at Lifepatch, Muhammad Zeian engaged with an interdisciplinary environment where art, science, and technology converge through collective learning and experimentation. Rooted in DIY and DIWO principles, Lifepatch provided a platform for exchanges with artists, researchers, activists, and technologists from diverse backgrounds, fostering new perspectives on collaborative practice, open-source culture, and community-based knowledge production. These residency experiences played a significant role in expanding his understanding of the relationship between technology, society, and artistic practice, while informing his ongoing work as an artist, facilitator, and cultural practitioner.

title: Asana Bina Seni
description: Asana Bina Seni 2023: (Se)tempat was an interdisciplinary learning and incubation program organized by the Yogyakarta Biennale Foundation that encouraged emerging artists to critically examine the relationship between place, identity, and contemporary social realities. Through a series of seminars, discussions, mentoring sessions, and project development workshops, participants engaged with topics such as decolonization in global art discourse, the relationship between art and socio-political realities, artistic research methodologies, feminist perspectives in art, and interdisciplinary artistic practices. Complemented by studio visits, proposal-writing workshops, artist statement development, and incubation sessions, the program provided a platform for participants to refine their artistic inquiries and develop projects rooted in their immediate contexts. Responding to the theme (Se)tempat, artists were invited to use local experiences and environments as starting points for exploring broader cultural, social, and political issues through contemporary art practice.

title: MEMEMASAK
description: MEMEMASAK was a collaborative workshop and artistic incubation program organized by Kapital Space that explored memes as a contemporary medium for communication, knowledge sharing, cultural critique, and artistic production. Through a series of discussions, presentations, collective research, and creative experiments, participants examined how memes shape communities, circulate information, construct identities, and influence public opinion. Drawing from internet culture, visual language, and everyday social phenomena, the workshop encouraged participants to critically engage with meme culture and translate their findings into original artistic projects. Emphasizing experimentation, dialogue, and collective learning, MEMEMASAK positioned the meme not only as a form of entertainment but also as a powerful tool for cultural reflection and creative practice.

title: Rembug Kliwon: Managerial
description: Rembug Kliwon: Managerial Class was an intensive discussion-based learning program that brought together artists, cultural workers, organizers, and collective practitioners to explore the challenges and possibilities of sustaining artistic and community-driven initiatives. Through a series of lectures, workshops, case studies, and open discussions with practitioners from across Indonesia, participants engaged with topics such as collective organization, community engagement, arts management, project development, activism, fundraising, and cultural ecosystems. Emphasizing collaboration, critical reflection, and knowledge sharing, the program provided a platform for emerging cultural practitioners to develop practical strategies for building sustainable artistic practices and socially engaged creative communities.

title: XPLORE New Media Art Incubation
description: XPLORE: New Media Art Incubation was an intensive workshop and incubation program that introduced participants to the diverse practices of contemporary media art through a combination of lectures, discussions, field visits, and hands-on experimentation. Organized across Jakarta and Yogyakarta, the program brought together artists, curators, researchers, and technologists to explore topics ranging from data-driven art, open-source hardware, and analogue electronics to portfolio development, artist writing, and sustainable creative practices. Through collaborative learning, mentorship, community visits, and project consultations, participants were encouraged to develop their artistic ideas while building the technical, conceptual, and professional skills necessary for contemporary media art practice.

title: Titen Waft Lab
description: TITEN (Teliti lan Telaten) was a five-day Light Art Workshop organized by Waft Lab in Surabaya, Indonesia, with support from the Ministry of Education and Culture through the Directorate of Media Arts. Designed as an intensive learning program, the workshop introduced participants to the fundamentals of light art, combining artistic exploration with technical skills in electronics, programming, and digital media. Through hands-on sessions, participants learned to control addressable LEDs using microcontrollers, computers, and network-based systems, while experimenting with light as a creative medium. The workshop encouraged interdisciplinary collaboration and provided an accessible platform for artists, students, and makers to explore the possibilities of interactive and computational light-based artworks.
